hints.title: Single Cycle Simulation
hints.text: Simulate the instructions exactly once from origin (0, 0) facing north. The displacement and ending orientation determine whether repeating instructions stays bounded.

hints.title: Orientation Invariance
hints.text: If the robot returns to (0, 0), it is trivially in a circle. If the robot does not face north after one cycle, four cycles will cancel out the linear displacement.

hints.title: Condition for Bounded Trajectory
hints.text: The trajectory remains bounded if and only if (x == 0 and y == 0) or the ending direction vector is not (0, 1). Return true if this holds, else false.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating arbitrary numbers of cycles without orientation invariants can loop indefinitely.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Simulating instructions once in O(N) time and O(1) space reveals the periodic behavior.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that non-north orientation guarantees a closed trajectory in 2 or 4 cycles.
complexity.notes: Rotations: left (dx, dy) -> (-dy, dx); right (dx, dy) -> (dy, -dx).
